blocks.text: Zscaler records session information for every admin who signs in to the Zscaler Admin Console. The audit log displays an admin's sign-in and sign-out attempts, actions, request ID, etc., including any configuration changes they completed during their session. Audit logs are stored for up to 6 months.
Audit logs provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: View session information for every admin who signs in to the Zscaler Admin Console.
View changes to the Private Access (ZPA) configuration.

blocks.text: The Zscaler Admin Console no longer has the Health Check setting for application segments, but healthCheckType can still appear in the audit logs.
On the Private Access page (Data Explorer> Audit Logs > Private Access), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Click the Calendar icon () to select a preset date range, or specify a custom start and end date. Admin audit log records are displayed in the table by the specified date range. By default, this is set to 6 Months.

View a list of applied filters available from the current and previous user sessions. Applied filters must be saved to the user session first before they can be viewed. Use the drop-down menu to select the applied filters to view. To learn more, see Using Tables.
Hide the filters on the page by clicking Hide Filters. Click Show Filters to display the filters.
Refresh the Audit Logs page to reflect the most current information.

Download the admin audit log records as a CSV file. Only admins with the Private Access Administrator role can download audit logs. The CSV file only includes audit log records for the time range and filters specified. Make sure that your filters are properly applied before clicking Download.

The time displayed is based on the time you choose for your account setting in the Zscaler Admin Console, but the exported CSV file (audit.csv) always lists the timestamp in UTC. Also, the Post-Configuration Change Value column within the CSV file uses a dollar sign ($) to separate the content within a cell.

Filter the admin audit log records. To filter the table by this information, select the appropriate option from the drop-down menu (e.g., Resource Type) or enter the proper value in the field (e.g., Resource Name), and click Apply. If one or more values are selected for the Admin ID or Client ID filters, only the logs related to either Admin ID or Client ID are shown in the table. For example, if you are filtering by Client ID, only client IDs are shown in the table even if All is selected for Admin ID. You can also save applied filters to your preferences so that they're visible in future user sessions. To learn more, see Using Tables.

For Managed Security Service Provider (MSSP) partners accessing the Zscaler Admin Console, if an admin views a child account for your organization, any configuration changes made appear in the Audit Logs page of the child account. However, the logs for the Authentication resource type are displayed within the Audit Logs page of the parent account. To learn more, see Signing In to the Zscaler Admin Console. The audit logs of the child account are captured when a parent account makes any changes in the child account. As soon as the parent account switches to the child account, a logging event is captured in the logs of the child account. Similarly, if a parent account makes any changes (e.g., to the child account configuration or policies), the logging events are captured in the child account.
View a list of session information for every admin that signs into the Zscaler Admin Console. For each admin audit log record, you can see:
Timestamp: The date and time of the admin's action. The time displayed is based on the time you choose for your account setting in the Zscaler Admin Console.
Admin ID: The admin's sign-in ID (or username).
Client ID: The API key's client ID that made changes via the API.
Action: The action performed by the admin or via the API.
View a list of all potential actions.
Learn more about the pre- and post-configuration changes for each action.

Within the Action column, click the () icon to view the differences between the pre- and post-configuration changes related to an action. You can also click Download to save a JSON file (audit-config.json) that includes the pre- and post-configuration change values.

For policy configuration changes, if any criteria (e.g., SAML Attribute, Application Segments, Segment Groups, etc.) is set to Any, Private Access records the action but the configuration change details do not explicitly display Any for the changed criteria. For example, the following policy had its SAML Attribute setting set to Any SAML Attribute when it was created, then it was updated to include a segment group. Click the () icon to view Create, Update, and Delete changes.

The Action is logged as well as any Resource Type associations made during that action. For example, when an admin creates a server and a server group within the Zscaler Admin Console, that server must be associated with a server group, and that server group must be associated with an App Connector group. So, both Server Group to Server Association and Server Group to App Connector Group Association are displayed under Resource Type.
You can then view the pre- and post-configuration change details for each.
Click the () icon to view Sign In and Sign Out attempt details.
Resource Type: The location within the Zscaler Admin Console or via the API where the action was performed.

For Timestamp, Admin ID, Action, and Resource Type, you can search for a specific text string or click Clear All to remove any selections within the drop-down menu.

Transaction ID: The unique identifier that binds multiple related API requests to assist in troubleshooting API request issues. Transaction IDs are created by the OneAPI framework. To learn more, see OneAPI Authentication in Authentication Service.
The Transaction ID column is only visible if Authentication Service is enabled for your organization.
Resource Name: The object name within a Resource Type (e.g., a policy name). Click the Copy icon to copy the name to your clipboard.
Request ID: The ID associated with the configuration change related to the action performed. Click the Copy icon to copy the ID to your clipboard.
